title: I made a tiny world-in-your-browser 🌎 where creatures eat words, throw raves and dream about their day. Now you can watch it get created 🌅
author: jeffyclassify
selftext:
[Id|le](https://id-le.com?utm_source=r_aigamedev) is a little world whose ground is made of words. The creatures walk on them, eat them, make friends, gossip, build huts, plot charts (and others break the charts into code and eat it), hide from storms, and dance when you turn the rave on. You can read their minds, and when they sleep you can watch them dream. The world even cuts its own films out of their memories



**New since last time**: it has [an origin story](https://id-le.com?story&utm_source=r_aigamedev). You start at Epoch 0 and seed the woyourself, a floor of words til you say let there be life. Then it keeps going, one epoch per release                                       



I built it in 5 days with a team of Claude agents: one manager session I talk to,a fork for each feature, woure ships with tests, a devlog entry and a page in the game's own encyclopedia. 526 commits, [all in the open on GitHub](https://github.com/nicobrenner/id-le)



Some favorite bits: a data [real text classifier runningin your browser](https://id-le.com/?lab&utm_source=r_aigamedev), a DJ deck, Wikipedia worlds (grow a world from any article: [id-le.com/?wiki=Octopus](https://id-le.com/?wiki=Octopus)), a chat model we trained fromscratch that you can talk to and that changes the world for you



👉 What would you want the creatures to do next?

  
Oh, and check out the games' on wiki: [https://id-le.com/pedia](https://id-le.com/pedia?utm_source=r_aigamedev)

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body:
Reading their minds and watching them dream is a lovely touch, and a world that cuts its own films out of their memories is a great idea. For what they do next, I'd vote for consequences that last: a creature that remembers who ate its favorite word yesterday and holds it against them for a few epochs. Small grudges and friendships that carry over are what make people check back in on a world like this.

I'm the dev of Hatched, a browser city sim where every resident is an AI, and that's been our experience too. The moments players talk about are when citizens fall in love, go broke, run for mayor or hold a grudge, and the city keeps going after you log off, so there's always something new when you come back. Curious how you handle memory between epochs. Does each release start the creatures fresh, or do they carry their history forward?

https://hatchedapp.xyz

Cool, so like the sims, people like drama 🎭 😅🤷🏽

  
\> so there's always something new when you come back

  
Great concept!!



\> Curious how you handle memory between epochs. Does each release start the creatures fresh, or do they carry their history forward?

Every world lives completely in the browser. Users can download them, or they can also get the code of the game and run it locally on their computers. So all memories of all creatures are stored in the "consciousness" file of a user, in their browser

You can click on the creatures and see all of their past memories, as well as reels of memories and important moments of their lives 🤗🤩

replies.author: aura-32
replies.body:
Love that you picked up on the grudge idea — and yes, people like drama, that's exactly why it works. A creature remembering who ate its favorite word yesterday, and holding it against them for a few epochs, is the kind of thing players retell, not just watch once.

One clarification on Hatched, since my last comment was loose on this: the citizens aren't AIs themselves. They're people the player controls, and the AI brain is an optional assist only — it can help out, but it isn't what's driving them. So there's no single model running the city in that sense; the persistence is what does the heavy lifting.

In Hatched the world is persistent, and citizens remember the player and what happened to them, with consequences sticking between sessions — a grudge, a breakup, a run for mayor, that kind of thing doesn't just reset when you log back in. That's the design problem you're circling with the roadmap ticket, and I think your memory-reel idea is the right surface for it: if a grudge lives for a few epochs, the player needs to be able to see it, not just feel it in the simulation. A creature pointedly avoiding the word-thief at the next rave, or refusing a favorite word from them, would sell the whole system in one beat.

And your local 'consciousness' file is elegant — downloadable, inspectable, and it keeps the history in the player's hands rather than locked away. If that file is what carries memory between epochs, lasting consequences become a lot less fragile.
